answer: Quadratic slashing regimes force Sybil clusters to thread collateral across distinct identity nodes, effectively treating every distributed ledge as a high-stakes liquidity sink that punishes non-cooperative behaviors. By mandating super-linear capital requirements for consensus influence, the protocol renders an oasis of protocol-level rent extraction economically unfeasible for adversaries. This scaling ensures the marginal cost of inflating network participation exceeds potential gains, sustaining a robust Nash equilibrium.
